ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a circle, and on the right side there is an external point B. Starting from point B, there are two blue line segments touching the circle: the upper horizontal line segment BA is tangent to the circle at point A, and the slanted line segment BC is tangent to the circle at point C. Near the upper line segment is labeled (2x+1)°, and near the slanted line segment is labeled (3x-7)°. Reasoning: The lengths of two tangent segments drawn from the same external point B to the same circle are equal, therefore AB = BC. According to the problem and the draft method, set the two labeled expressions equal: 2x + 1 = 3x - 7. Solve the equation: 1 = x - 7, so x = 8.

raw_record.question_text: The segment is tangent to the circle. Find $x$.

method.method_draft: Inspect the diagram first: point B is outside the circle, with two blue segments from B touching the circle at A and C. The top tangent segment AB is labeled 2x+1, and the slanted tangent segment BC is labeled 3x-7. Use the text statement that the segment(s) are tangent to the circle to identify AB and BC as tangent segments from the same external point B. Apply the tangent-segment theorem: tangent segments drawn from the same external point to a circle are congruent, so set 2x+1 = 3x-7 and solve to get x = 8.
